content: 1. Urban and rural areas can be classified based on population distribution in physical spaces, with or without access to essential services. In some cases, urban areas are defined first, and rural areas are determined by exclusion. 2. In many countries, population size or density is the standard criterion for defining rurality, such as a low number of inhabitants in a given land area. 3. Local administrative units may include a mix of urban and rural populations. Urban areas can be defined using multiple criteria, such as cities, municipalities, or metropolitan areas, while rural areas are defined by default as those not meeting urban criteria. 4. Self-sufficiency in the health workforce involves strategic investment in national infrastructure to achieve an optimal, stable, and appropriately distributed health workforce. This is achieved through effective recruitment and retention policies and programs. 5. Sex refers to the biological determination of an individual’s sex at birth. 6. Skill mix refers to the combination or grouping of different categories of staff in the workforce, their roles, and activities. It also describes the mix of posts, grades, or occupations within an organization. In healthcare, it includes the combination of skills available at a specific time, the mix of posts in a facility, the mix of employees in a post, the activities within each role, and differences across occupational groups such as nurses and physicians or within a single group, such as different types of nursing providers with varying levels of training and wages. 7. Social accountability is the obligation of an authorized body to direct its education, research, and service activities toward addressing the priority health concerns of the community, region, or nation it serves. 8. Social determinants of health are the conditions in which people are born, grow, work, live, and age, as well as the broader forces and systems shaping these conditions. These include economic policies, development agendas, social norms, social policies, and political systems. 9. The specialist surgical workforce includes licensed and qualified physician surgeons, anesthesiologists, and obstetricians. 10. A student is an individual who is not economically active and attends a regular educational institution, either public or private, for systematic instruction at any level of education. 11. Subnational levels are defined based on the specific conditions, governing structures, and constitutional provisions of a given country. Administrative boundaries are disaggregated to the first or second subnational level, such as states, regions, provinces, counties, or districts, without overlaps between administrative units. 12. Expenditure on mandatory continuing professional development should be included within social contributions. 13. Total public expenditure on health workforce education refers to current and capital expenditure expressed as a percentage of gross national income (GNI) or gross national product (GNP) in a given financial year. This indicator reflects the proportion of income spent by government authorities on health workforce education. It can also be calculated based on gross domestic product (GDP). 14. Total expenditure on healthcare includes current health expenditure plus capital investment in healthcare infrastructure. 15. Total public health expenditure includes current public health expenditure and capital investment in healthcare infrastructure. 16. Transformative health workforce education refers to the sustainable expansion and reform of health workforce education and training to increase the quantity, quality, and relevance of health workers. This strengthens national health systems and improves population health outcomes. 17. Tuition fees are the money students pay to health workforce education and training institutions for their teaching. 18. Unemployment refers to all working-age individuals who are qualified for a job, are not employed, have actively sought employment during a specified recent period, and are currently available to take up employment if an opportunity arises. 19. The vacancy rate is the proportion of total posts that are vacant, expressed as a percentage of all positions, both filled and unfilled.
